question: In which of the following years was the Railway budget merged with the Union budget?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2017**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget took effect from the financial year 2017-18.
 
• This decision was made by the Narendra Modi government, based on recommendations from a committee headed by NITI Aayog member Bibek Debroy.
 
• The historic practice of presenting a separate Railway Budget, which had been in place since 1924, was discontinued.
 
• The merger aimed to streamline the budgetary process and eliminate the need for separate presentations and discussions.
 
• It was argued that the separate Railway Budget had become redundant and was hindering the overall financial management of the country.
 
• By merging the budgets, the government aimed to integrate the railways' financial planning with the national economic strategy.
 
• The merger also sought to eliminate the political populism associated with the Railway Budget, where announcements of new trains and projects were often made for electoral gains.
 
• It was intended to bring greater financial discipline to the railways and improve their operational efficiency.
 
• The merger allowed for better utilization of resources and eliminated the need for the railways to pay an annual dividend to the government.
 
• The merger was also designed to remove artificial divisions that had existed in the government's financial planning.
 
• The merger brought the railway expenditure and revenue into the main financial statement of the government.
 
• The merger made it easier to implement a holistic transport policy.
 
• The merger helps to remove the railways from being a separate financial entity, and make it part of the overall government financial structure.
 
• The merger was a result of the changing economic landscape of India.
 
• The merger has allowed for a more focused approach to railway development.
 
• The merger has allowed for more long term planning for the railway network.
 
• The merger has helped to improve the financial health of the railways.
 
• The merger has allowed for greater flexibility in the allocation of funds to the railways.
 
• The merger has helped to reduce the administrative burden on the government.
